Driver state monitoring

A fusion-based approach to drowsiness mitigation: a real-time system that cross-checks a camera against the driver’s seat and an accelerometer.

The problem

Fatigued drivers cause about 100,000 crashes a year in the U.S. Most driver monitoring relies on simple image processing or vehicle data, which only flags drowsiness after dangerous driving has started.

What I built

After a decision matrix ruled out vehicle input and EEG, I fused three low-cost sensors: eye-closure detection from an ArduCam running a YOLOv8 model, force-sensing resistors in the seat that catch postural slumps, and an accelerometer. Any one can be fooled; together they’re robust.

Results

Fusion was significantly more accurate than any single sensor (Fisher’s exact test, p < 0.05) and held up across lighting changes (p < 0.01) and eyewear like sunglasses (p < 0.05). Mean latency of 473.88 ms was significantly faster than human perception (p < 0.0001).

Next steps: a more diverse training dataset, a wireless accelerometer, heart-rate monitoring, and haptic alerts like seat or steering-wheel vibration.
